# Adjudication Task — Chapter 289

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃289화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“네?”
  6|
  7|최 팀장의 얼굴에는 지금까지 본 적 없는, 크고 격렬한 동요가 일어나고 있었다.
  8|
  9|그나마 침착해 보이는 김 집사도 크게 다르지는 않았다.
 10|
 11|아직 가시지 않은 분함와 얼떨떨함. 그리고 내 말에 대한 의문.
 12|
 13|‘저런 표정도 지을 수 있었나.’
 14|
 15|내가 앞뒤 가리지 않고 앞서나갈 때, 언제나 침착하게 두 걸음 물러서서 사태를 수습하던 두 사람이었다.
 16|
 17|이제야 그나마 나와 같은 사람으로 보인다.
 18|
 19|나는 묘한 감흥을 느끼며 입을 열었다.
 20|
 21|“답은 간단해요. 적들이 강하다면 우리도 강해지면 됩니다.”
 22|
 23|“진태경 씨.”
 24|
 25|최 팀장의 목소리는 조용했고 흔들림이 없었다. 처음의 감정을 수습한 그는 다시 침착한 평소의 모습으로 돌아와 있었다.
 26|
 27|“이건 답을 안다고 해서 해결되는 수학 문제가 아닙니다. 정답에 도달하기 위해서는 상상할 수도 없을 만큼 힘든 과정을 거쳐야 해요.”
 28|
 29|“그럼 괜찮네요. 내가 과외 선생 역할로 붙으면 시간이 걸리더라도 풀 수는 있을 것 같은데. 아, 대신 과목은 바꿉시다. 수학은 젬병이라서.”
 30|
 31|“잊으셨습니까? 상대는 아레스 길드예요. 진태경 씨는 모르지만 저는 알고 있습니다. 그들이 얼마나 강한 상대인지.”
 32|
 33|“안타깝지만 도련님의 말씀이 맞습니다.”
 34|
 35|최 팀장과 김 집사는 그 말을 끝으로 입을 다물었다.
 36|
 37|한 사람은 아레스 길드장 천태민의 외손자, 다른 한 사람은 그 천태민을 오랫동안 모신 핵심 인물이다.
 38|
 39|그들의 위치가 위치인 만큼 직접 보고, 겪은 일들이 많을 것이다. 끓어오르는 가슴과는 달리 냉철한 두뇌는 이미 답을 계산해 냈다. 하지만…….
 40|
 41|“최 팀장님.”
 42|
 43|이미 마침표가 찍혀 있는 그의 눈동자를 들여다보며 물었다.
 44|
 45|“명동 길드로 가기 전 나한테 했던 말, 기억납니까?”
 46|
 47|“물론입니다.”
 48|
 49|“그때 뭐라고 했어요?”
 50|
 51|잠시 머뭇거리던 최 팀장이 입술을 뗐다.
 52|
 53|“진태경 씨는 언뜻 보면 무모해 보이지만…….”
 54|
 55|“항상 최악의 상황을 예상하고 움직인다. 그리고?”
 56|
 57|“늘 최선의 결과를 갖고 온다.”
 58|
 59|“최 팀장님 본인보다 날 더 믿는다면서요? 그거 그냥 듣기 좋으라고 한 소리였습니까?”
 60|
 61|“그건 절대 아닙니다.”
 62|
 63|“내가 공부는 못했어도, 가능성 제로인 게임에 목숨 걸고 덤벼들 만큼 멍청한 놈은 아닙니다. 이거, 할 만해요.”
 64|
 65|“할 만하다…….”
 66|
 67|“최 팀장님 본인을 못 믿겠으면 저를 믿으세요.”
 68|
 69|내 말에 실린 진심을 느낀 최 팀장의 눈동자에 빛이 스며든다. 비록 희미했지만, 그 빛의 정체는 희망이었다.
 70|
 71|희망은 불씨와 같다. 타오르는 것도, 사그라드는 것도 모두 한순간이다. 불씨가 꺼지기 전에 풀무질을 해 줘야 한다.
 72|
 73|“말이 나왔으니까 말인데, 내가 여기서 길드 나가면 최 팀장님도 포기할 겁니까? 뭐, 길드 접고 은퇴해서 김 집사님이랑 농사짓는 것도 나쁘진 않네요. 그렇게 되면 이정룡이 비료도 지원해 주겠네.”
 74|
 75|“진태경 헌터님!”
 76|
 77|나를 가로막으려는 김 집사를 무시하고 말을 이어갔다.
 78|
 79|“세계 최고의 길드를 만들고 싶다면서요. 나 내보내고, 꺽정 아저씨랑 송이도 보내고. 새로 받아들인 신입들까지 떠나면 두 분께서 아레스 길드와 싸울 생각입니까?”
 80|
 81|“…….”
 82|
 83|“최 팀장님.”
 84|
 85|묵묵부답. 대답은 돌아오지 않았다.
 86|
 87|그러나 눈동자에 스며든 불씨는 아직 죽지 않았다.
 88|
 89|이내 그의 입술 사이로 잠긴 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 90|
 91|“아레스 길드는 하나의 제국입니다. 국내 10대 길드가 힘을 합쳐도 당해 내지 못할 만큼 강력한 제국 말입니다.”
 92|
 93|“어이구, 그놈들 따라잡으려면 부지런히 움직여야겠네.”
 94|
 95|“아레스 길드의 전부까지는 아니더라도, 상당 부분을 알고 있습니다. 그래서 더 위험하다고 생각하는 거고요.”
 96|
 97|“동시에 가능성이 더 올라갔네요. 적을 잘 파악하고 있다는 거니까. 지피지기백전불태(知彼知己百戰不殆). 맞죠?”
 98|
 99|“몇 번이나 생각해 봤지만 제 계산의 답은 불가능이었습니다.”
100|
101|“그럼 다시 계산해 보세요.”
102|
103|“정말…… 가능합니까?”
104|
105|“네.”
106|
107|“어디에서 제 계산이 틀린 겁니까? 도대체 어떤 것이 진태경 씨의 답에 확신을 갖게 한 겁니까?”
108|
109|이해하지 못했기에 묻는 것이 아니다. 최 팀장은 누구보다 자신의 답이 틀렸기를 바란다. 이정룡과 맞서 싸울 수 있는 실낱같은 가능성을 원한다.
110|
111|나는 그의 바람에 기꺼이 대답해 주었다.
112|
113|“지금 팀장님과 이야기를 나누고 있는 사람.”
114|
115|“……!”
116|
117|“팀장님의 계산 과정은 정확했습니다. 한 가지만 빼면요.”
118|
119|천천히 손가락을 들어, 내 가슴을 가리켰다.
120|
121|“바로 접니다.”
122|
123|그 순간, 최 팀장의 눈동자가 흔들렸다. 그 안에 스며 있던 불씨가 사그라드는 것이 느껴졌다.
124|
125|빈자리를 차지한 것은 희망이 아닌 실망감이었다.
126|
127|“제 계산에는 진태경 씨도 포함되어 있었습니다.”
128|
129|“그랬겠죠. 내가 아는 팀장님이라면.”
130|
131|최 팀장은 명석한 사람이다. 타고난 리더십에 뛰어난 안목과 추진력도 갖췄다.
132|
133|냉정한 마음으로 평화 길드와 아레스 길드를 한 저울추에 올려놨고, 평화 길드가 가진 무게에는 나도 포함되어 있었을 것이다.
134|
135|“지금까지 진태경 씨가 보여 준 모습은 항상 놀라웠습니다. 아니, 경이로울 정도였어요.”
136|
137|나는 그의 흐려지는 목소리 뒤에 어떤 말이 따라올지 이미 알고 있다.
138|
139|“그렇지만 부족하다?”
140|
141|최 팀장이 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
142|
143|“아레스 길드에는 S급 헌터인 이정룡을 제외하고도 백 명이 넘는 A급 헌터가 정식으로 소속되어 있습니다. 중, 하급 헌터는 수도 없이 많죠.”
144|
145|최 팀장이 ‘정식으로’라는 단어에 유난히 힘을 주는 것은 알려지지 않은 전력이 더 있다는 뜻이다.
146|
147|‘그런데도 A급 헌터만 백 명이 넘는다니.’
148|
149|이미 예전부터 풍문으로 들어 알고 있던 사실이지만, 최 팀장의 입을 통해 직접 들으니 아레스 길드가 가진 전력이 실감이 갔다.
150|
151|내가 아무리 강하다 한들 결국 하나의 손에 지나지 않으니 최 팀장의 판단은 냉철했다.
152|
153|그러나…….
154|
155|“그런 식이라면 계산 다시 하셔야겠는데요?”
156|
157|“네?”
158|
159|“공식은 맞는데 숫자가 틀렸네. 팀장님께서 나한테 매긴 값이 어느 정도인지는 모르겠지만 적어도 몇 배는 더 잡아야 할 텐데.”
160|
161|최 팀장은 물론이고 김 집사와 임꺽정, 송송이까지 눈을 부릅떴다.
162|
163|지금까지 내가 해낸 일들을 생각하면 그럴 만도 하다.
164|
165|단신으로 네임드 몬스터를 사냥하고, 서른에 달하는 블랙 헌터를 갈아 버렸으며 명동 길드라는 대형 길드와 정면으로 맞섰다.
166|
167|나는 석상처럼 굳어 버린 사람들을 뒤로하고 최 팀장을 응시했다.
168|
169|“누누이 얘기했던 것 같은데요. 나는 팀장님이 생각하는 것 이상으로 비밀이 많은 놈이라고.”
170|
171|무림은 무림, 현대는 현대.
172|
173|내 머릿속에는 두 세계를 구분하는 뚜렷한 경계선이 있었다. 하지만 이정룡이, 아레스 길드가 그 선을 지워 버렸다.
174|
175|아마 이번 같은 일이 없었더라면 나는 그 비밀을 평생 홀로 간직했을 것이다.
176|
177|‘조용히 살고 싶었던 건 너무 큰 욕심이었나?’
178|
179|어쩌면 이건 내게 주어진 힘의 숙명일지도 모르겠다. 그러니 이제는 받아들여야 한다. 언제까지나 피해 다닐 수는 없다.
180|
181|적들로부터 소중한 것들을 지키기 위해서는 강해져야 한다.
182|
183|“자, 이제 어떻게 하시겠어요?”
184|
185|최 팀장은 여전히 믿을 수 없다는 눈빛으로 나를 바라보고 있었다.
186|
187|“진태경 씨는 항상 저를 놀라게 만드는군요.”
188|
189|“아껴 둬요. 앞으로는 그런 일이 더 많을 테니까.”
190|
191|“위험한 길이 될 겁니다.”
192|
193|“내가 또 가시밭길 전문이라.”
194|
195|“지금까지와는 비교도 안 될 정도로요.”
196|
197|“비교가 안 되긴 무슨. 팀장님이 몰라서 그렇지 이쪽은 이미 지옥이야…….”
198|
199|내 말을 농담으로 알아들은 모양이다.
200|
201|나는 마침내 피식 웃음을 터트린 최 팀장을 물끄러미 바라보았다.
202|
203|“팀장님.”
204|
205|“네?”
206|
207|“가끔은 솔직해져도 괜찮습니다.”
208|
209|최 팀장의 입가에 맺혀 있던 웃음이 사라졌다. 눈빛은 가라앉고 입을 꽉 다물린다.
210|
211|나는 그가 입을 열기를 기다렸다. 지금부터 해야 하는 말은 최 팀장의 입으로 직접 들어야 한다.
212|
213|다행히 기다림은 그다지 길지 않았다.
214|
215|“외람된 부탁이지만 계속 평화 길드와 함께해 주시겠습니까?”
216|
217|그래. 이거지.
218|
219|나는 씩 웃으며 최 팀장의 어깨를 툭 쳤다. 겉보기에는 똑똑하고 냉정해 보이지만 아직 속이 여리다.
220|
221|내심 함께하고 싶으면서도 우리가 다칠 것을 우려해 내보내려 했던 이유도 이것 때문이다.
222|
223|“잘해 봅시다.”
224|
225|“……고맙습니다.”
226|
227|언뜻 미소를 지어 보인 최 팀장이 다른 사람들을 향해 돌아섰다.
228|
229|충복이자 한 핏줄이나 다름없는 사이인 김 집사가 가장 먼저 입을 열었다.
230|
231|“제 대답은 이미 알고 계실 거라 믿습니다.”
232|
233|“감사합니다, 김 집사님.”
234|
235|다음 차례는 송송이였다. 최 팀장으로부터 나와 같은 질문을 받은 그녀는 한숨을 푹푹 내쉬더니 입을 열었다.
236|
237|“아레스 길드라니. 아, 이건 좀 수지타산이 안 맞는데.”
238|
239|사실 이게 가장 정상적인 반응이다. 아레스 길드랑 대놓고 척을 지겠다는데 환영하는 놈이 있으면 이상하지.
240|
241|“수지타산에 맞게 연봉 두 배로 책정해 주세요. 생명 수당도.”
242|
243|“…….”
244|
245|송송이 얘도 정상은 아니구나.
246|
247|어이없는 표정으로 바라보자 그녀가 어깨를 으쓱했다.
248|
249|“왜, 뭐?”
250|
251|“아니, 그냥. 지금 같은 경우에는 보통은 그냥 나가지 않나?”
252|
253|“나갔으면 좋겠어?”
254|
255|“어허, 그건 절대 아니지.”
256|
257|“내가 왜 아레스 길드에서 평화 길드로 옮겼는지 알아? 그것도 사방에서 견제받는 최 팀장님을 따라서.”
258|
259|“나야 모르지.”
260|
261|“연봉 두 배로 챙겨 주신댔거든.”
262|
263|“…….”
264|
265|“내 목표가 나이 서른에 은퇴하는 거야. 남은 2년 동안 바짝 벌면 평생 풍족하게 살 수 있겠지.”
266|
267|아무렇지 않게 말하고 있지만, 자신도 함께하고 싶다는 말을 빙빙 돌린 것에 불과하다. 알뜰살뜰한 송송이가 이미 한 재산 모아 놨음을 모두가 알고 있다.
268|
269|“그리고 뭐, 너한테도 계획이 있는 것 같으니까 일단 믿어 보려고. 최 팀장님처럼 능력 좋고 잘생긴 상관 만나기도 힘들고.”
270|
271|어쨌든 이렇게 송송이의 잔류도 확정되었다. 나를 포함한 사람들의 시선이 마지막 한 명을 향해 움직였다.
272|
273|“꺽정 아저씨.”
274|
275|내 부름에도 대답이 없던 그는 한참 만에 입술을 뗐다.
276|
277|“태경아, 내가 도움이 될까?”
278|
279|“충분히요.”
280|
281|“고작 D급 헌터인데도?”
282|

Murim was Murim, and the modern world was the modern world.

[P89]
There had always been a clear boundary in my mind separating the two. But Lee Jungryong and Ares Guild had erased that line.

[P90]
If none of this had happened, I probably would have kept my secret for the rest of my life.

[P91]
*Was wanting to live quietly too much to ask?*

[P92]
Perhaps this was the fate that came with the power I had been given. If so, it was time to accept it. I couldn’t keep running forever.

[P93]
To protect the things precious to me from my enemies, I had to become stronger.

[P94]
“So, what are you going to do?”

[P95]
Team Leader Choi still stared at me in disbelief.

[P96]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, you never cease to surprise me.”

[P97]
“Save it. There’ll be plenty more surprises from now on.”

[P98]
“It will be a dangerous road.”

[P99]
“I happen to specialize in thorny roads.”

[P100]
“Far more dangerous than anything you’ve faced until now.”

[P101]
“Far more dangerous, my ass. You just don’t know it. This side is already hell…”

[P102]
He seemed to take my words as a joke.

[P103]
I quietly watched Team Leader Choi finally let out a short laugh.

[P104]
“Team Leader.”

[P105]
“Yes?”

[P106]
“Sometimes, it’s okay to be honest.”

[P107]
The smile vanished from the corners of Team Leader Choi’s mouth. His gaze settled, and his lips pressed into a firm line.

[P108]
I waited for him to speak. What came next was something I needed to hear directly from him.

[P109]
Fortunately, I didn’t have to wait long.

[P110]
“I know this is a presumptuous request, but… would you continue with Peace Guild?”

[P111]
*Yes. That was it.*

[P112]
I grinned and lightly tapped Team Leader Choi on the shoulder. He looked intelligent and cold on the outside, but he was softhearted underneath.

[P113]
That was why he had tried to send us away despite wanting us to stay. He was afraid we would get hurt.

[P114]
“Let’s make this work.”

[P115]
“……Thank you.”

[P116]
Team Leader Choi offered a fleeting smile before turning toward the others.

[P117]
Butler Kim—his devoted retainer and someone practically family—spoke first.

[P118]
“I trust you already know my answer.”

[P119]
“Thank you, Butler Kim.”

[P120]
Next was Song Song. When Team Leader Choi asked her the same question he had asked me, she heaved several deep sighs before answering.

[P121]
“Ares Guild? Ah, the numbers really don’t add up on this one.”

[P122]
Honestly, that was the most normal reaction. We were openly declaring our intention to make an enemy of Ares Guild. Anyone who welcomed the idea would be strange.

[P123]
“Double my annual salary. And add hazard pay.”

[P124]
“……”

[P125]
Song Song wasn’t normal either.

[P126]
When I stared at her in disbelief, she shrugged.

[P127]
“What? Why?”

[P128]
“No reason. I just thought most people would walk away in a situation like this.”

[P129]
“Do you want me to leave?”

[P130]
“Hey, absolutely not.”

[P131]
“Do you know why I transferred from Ares Guild to Peace Guild? Why I followed Team Leader Choi even with everyone trying to keep him down?”

[P132]
“How would I know?”

[P133]
“Because he promised to double my salary.”

[P134]
“……”

[P135]
“My goal is to retire at thirty. If I earn as much as I can over the next two years, I’ll be able to live comfortably for the rest of my life.”

[P136]
She spoke as though it were nothing, but this was only her roundabout way of saying she wanted to stay with us too. Everyone knew the frugal Song Song had already amassed a small fortune.

[P137]
“Besides, you seem to have a plan, so I’ll trust you for now. It isn’t easy to find a superior as capable and handsome as Team Leader Choi.”

[P138]
And just like that, Song Song’s decision to stay was settled. Everyone’s gaze, including mine, shifted toward the last person.

[P139]
“Uncle Kkeokjeong.”

[P140]
He didn’t answer when I called him. Only after a long silence did he finally speak.

[P141]
“Taekyung, will I be any help?”

[P142]
“More than enough.”

[P143]
“Even though I’m only a D-rank Hunter?”

[P144]
“People with D in their names are always the real protagonists. Why not legally change yours while you’re at it? Im D. Kkeokjeong. What do you think?”

[P145]
Im Kkeokjeong burst out laughing, then looked Team Leader Choi straight in the eye.

[P146]
“It wasn’t your fault I got hurt, Team Leader Choi. So don’t blame yourself.”

[P147]
“No. It was all my fault. Please focus on your recovery and rehabilitation first, then take your time thinking it over. You have a family, Hunter Im.”

[P148]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P149]
“Yes?”

[P150]
“Do you know what my first thought was when my arms were cut off?”

[P151]
“Your family?”

[P152]
He was a husband and the father of two children.

[P153]
But Im Kkeokjeong calmly shook his head.

[P154]
“*Ah, I guess I can’t work as a Hunter anymore.* That was the first thing that came to mind.”

[P155]
“……”

[P156]
“I love this work. I spent twenty years going in and out of Gates not merely to earn a living, but because I felt a sense of duty as a Hunter. But…”

[P157]
Im Kkeokjeong bit down hard on his lip. His gaze remained fixed on his bandaged arms.

[P158]
“Can I recover?”

[P159]
“You can. You will.”

[P160]
A faint smile spread across Im Kkeokjeong’s lips.

[P161]
“Then I’m coming too. I can’t abandon a Hunter’s duty over something like this.”

[P162]
Something stirred deep in my chest at the sight.

[P163]
People dismissed him as a low-rank Hunter in name only, but Im Kkeokjeong was one of the few true Hunters left in this age.

[P164]
*They’re all far too good to stop here.*

[P165]
All right. Strike while the iron was hot.

[P166]
Having made up my mind, I opened my Skill Window for the first time in ages.

[P167]
There, among the densely packed entries in the holographic window, I found what I wanted.

[P168]
> **System**
>
> **Skill:** Martial Arts Manual Creation

[P169]
*Yes. This was the beginning.*

[P170]
With firm resolve, I touched the holographic window.

[P171]
Beep!

[P172]
> **System**
>
> To create a martial arts manual, you need at least 300 sheets of A4 paper!

[P173]
“……”

[P174]
What the fuck.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
